answer.answer:
**Summary**

The one documented route to circularity in concrete work is to design the connections so elements can come apart: glued and monolithic joints are what destroy salvage value, and reversible connection design is what recovers it, which for cast-in-place concrete is the whole difficulty. That route has a single requirement in front of me, component-level traceable data or material passports, without which recovered elements are not economically worth reusing, and a single documented payoff, material and energy saving with reduced CO2 and waste. The asymmetry is the finding: 26 of the 50 coded cases already carry the traceable-data layer but only 8 carry circular construction, so the enabling data exists far more widely than the design practice that would use it. No deployed case in the material in front of me is coded for concrete circularity, and the circularity evidence here is general to construction rather than specific to cast-in-place, precast or shotcrete work, so treat it as a design principle rather than a proven concrete workflow.

**Detailed answer**

*The mechanism, and its single requirement*

Circular construction/DfDisAssembly (VA15) carries exactly one inbound and one outbound dependency edge, both listed in full, so this is the complete documented picture for it, and it is a thin one. VA15 carries 1 inbound and 1 outbound dependency edge, and 8 of the 50 coded cases draw on it. [1]

Upstream, the requirement is data. Allow traceable/linked data (VA9) enablesCapability Circular construction/DfDisAssembly (VA15), on the mechanism that component data and material passports make recovery and reuse economically viable [2], on peer-reviewed evidence. 26 of the 50 coded cases draw on VA9 [1], three times the 8 that reach circular construction, so the constraint in practice is not the availability of linked data but the decision to design for recovery on top of it.

Downstream, the payoff is material. VA15 enablesCapability Material/energy saving/reduce CO2/waste (VA4), because glued and monolithic joints limit salvage potential while reversible connection design under DfDisAssembly enables material recovery [3], again peer-reviewed. That sentence is the operative advice for concrete: the monolithic pour is precisely the joint type named as limiting salvage, which pushes the answer toward precast or demountable connection detailing rather than cast-in-place continuity. 15 of the 50 coded cases draw on VA4. [1]

*A second, indirect argument for the data layer*

Traceable data does more than unlock disassembly. VA9 mitigates Increase cost/investment uncertainty (RI3), on the mechanism that material passports reduce uncertainty about the circular potential and economics of disassembled elements. [1] 13 of the 50 coded cases draw on RI3. [1] This matters because RI3 is also among the enablers most often appearing alongside circular construction in the coded cases, at a weight of 6 (Increase cost/investment uncertainty (RI3), weight 6) [4]. That pairing is statistical co-occurrence, not an asserted dependency, so read it as: circular cases tend to be cases where cost uncertainty is also a live issue, and the material-passport route is the one documented lever against it.

*What tends to sit alongside circular work, without being claimed as a cause*

The co-occurrence profile for VA15 is a correlation across cases and asserts no direction. The enablers most often co-occurring with VA15 include Material testing (PR10) at weight 8, Integrate supply chain (VA14) at weight 7, and Modularisation (PR5), Excavation/transportation (PR16), Early contractor involvement (CO11) and DfMA for DFAB process (PR9) at weight 6 each, with Subtractive manufacturing (PR7) and CNC machines (RE7) at weight 4 and Increase material usage/waste (RI16) at weight 3. [4] There are 125 co-occurring enablers in total [4], so this is a cut, not a closed list, and none of these should be read as a precondition for circularity: the graph asserts no dependency edge from any of them into VA15.

Modularisation and DfMA are worth flagging anyway because they do carry asserted edges elsewhere that point at the same detailing logic. Modularisation (PR5) enablesCapability Mass-customisation (PR11) via modular building-blocks [5], and DfMA for DFAB process (PR9) enablesCapability Modularisation (PR5) [1]. 15 of the 50 coded cases draw on PR9 [1] and 10 draw on PR5 [1]. Those edges are about customisation and production, not recovery, so use them as adjacent practice, not as a circularity claim.

*Deployed record and coverage*

There is no Process RP record and no census record in the material in front of me linking a deployed concrete project to circular construction, so nothing here rests on a fielded case: the two circularity edges are both literature. Retrieval also widened "concrete construction" onto the generic circularity node rather than onto cast-in-place, precast or shotcrete categories, which means the salvage argument is stated for built structures in general and the concrete-specific verification is not present here.

One adjacent point for printed concrete specifically, since it is the concrete process the context does treat: Additive manufacturing (PR3) dependsOn Regulatory/legal concern (RI18), because 3D printed concrete walls require certification against acceptance criteria for structural strength, fire safety and durability [6], on standards evidence. 4 of the 50 coded cases draw on PR3 [1] and 12 draw on RI18 [1]. That is a compliance gate on printed concrete, not a circularity route, and the context establishes no edge between additive manufacturing and circular construction.

*What to do*

Put the component-level data layer in first, since it is the only documented requirement and is already present in half the coded record. Then move the detailing decision: substitute reversible connections for glued and monolithic joints wherever the structural scheme allows, which is the specific act the evidence credits with recovering material. Expect the return in material and energy saving rather than in schedule or cost directly; no edge in front of me runs from circular construction to time, productivity or cost. And treat the rarity honestly: at 8 of 50 cases, this is a minority practice in the coded record, and the evidence supporting it here is a single peer-reviewed source read through two edges.
